- When sentiment is positive (1.00) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (-1.00) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model consistently under-estimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply a small upward bias to early periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below the peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- Mean reversion is evident in late horizon (days 20–30) — model often over-optimistically forecasts upward trends; reduce forecast slope or apply downward drag if sentiment is neutral or weak.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1 and -1, model tends to lag by 1–2 days; adjust forecast to anticipate sentiment shifts 1–2 days ahead.
